question: Which trim mode should a btrfs SSD use: discard=sync, discard=async or periodic fstrim?
statement: Do not recommend discard=sync: it trims freed extents immediately, and fragmented ranges may cause a severe performance hit. discard=async is described as an improved version of synchronous trim; it tracks freed extents in memory, then starts after a period or when enough ranges accumulate, expecting larger ranges and throttling the number of I/O requests so other filesystem activity is not disrupted. Manual fstrim needs no mount options, traverses free space across the filesystem, and suits a periodic service; periodic trimming may also prevent unexpected slowdown from device-internal data relocation. Since kernel 6.2, the discard=async mount option is automatically enabled for devices that support it. Trim is a device hint: it may be ignored, applied only to ranges meeting criteria, or skipped for other factors affecting memory cells.
